item.title: Mamdani calls ICE a 'rogue' agency after NYC shooting, claims agents view law as 'merely a suggestion'
item.description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani accused ICE of being a "rogue federal agency" after an immigration officer fired seven shots at a man in Manhattan.
item.content:encoded:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani accused Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) of operating as a "rogue federal agency" and treating the law as "merely a suggestion" during a Sunday interview, days after a federal immigration officer fired seven shots at a man in Manhattan while his 5-year-old son was inside the vehicle.

Mamdani, speaking to MS NOW host Jacob Soboroff in his first interview since Thursday's shooting of 28-year-old Oscar Belgal, accused ICE agents of repeatedly disregarding the law and questioned whether New Yorkers could distinguish federal officers from dangerous attackers.

"We follow the law in New York City and I know that to the secretary, the law is merely a suggestion when it comes to the actions of these ICE agents," Mamdani said. "They are making a mockery of what law and order is."

MAMDANI BLASTS FEDS FOR WAGING 'CAMPAIGN OF VIOLENCE AND TERROR' AGAINST NYC'S IMMIGRANTS

The Department of Homeland Security pushed back against Mamdani's accusations in a statement to Fox News Digital, defending ICE and criticizing the mayor's rhetoric toward federal immigration officers.

"ICE enforces the law as written. What makes someone a target for immigration enforcement is whether or not they are illegally in the U.S. — full stop," a DHS spokesperson said. "Mayor Mamdani should be thanking our law enforcement for removing these dangerous criminals from his city — NOT vilifying law enforcement."

"Attacks and demonization of ICE law enforcement is wrong," the statement continued. "Because of smears like this our ICE officers are now facing a 1,600% increase in assaults against them as they put their lives on the line to arrest murderers, rapists, pedophiles, gang members, and terrorists."

EXCLUSIVE: DHS SECRETARY MULLIN SLAMS SANCTUARY POLITICIANS AS ATTACKS ON ICE OFFICERS SKYROCKET

Mamdani argued that ICE's operations were making New Yorkers less safe and calling for the agency's elimination.

"What we see from their actions is an agency that terrorizes, one that creates a sense of fear as opposed to any idea of safety. And I made it very clear that the longer that ICE agents were engaging in their operations in the city, the less safe this city was becoming," Mamdani said.

The shooting occurred Thursday afternoon in the Marble Hill neighborhood, where ICE agents attempted to apprehend Belgal, a Dominican national whom DHS said had a prior grand larceny conviction and previous arrests involving assault, robbery, drugs and weapons.

NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch said at least one federal immigration officer fired seven rounds, striking Belgal in the neck below his left ear. His 5-year-old son, who was sitting inside the vehicle, was unharmed.

Mamdani said he spoke with President Donald Trump and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin for nearly two hours Thursday evening in an unsuccessful effort to secure Belgal's release. He expressed frustration with the secretary's assessment of the shooting.

"What struck me is the secretary did not think that ICE agents had done anything wrong," Mamdani said. "I am demanding that ICE cease their operations in our city immediately, because these operations make New Yorkers less safe. They leave New Yorkers in a state of terror."

DHS SECRETARY BASHES NEW YORK LEADERSHIP AFTER ANNOUNCING THOUSANDS OF ARRESTS IN SWEEPING OPERATION

On Friday, U.S. District Judge Paul Oetken temporarily blocked Belgal's deportation while his challenge to federal detention remains pending. The judge also restricted his transfer outside specified federal judicial districts without prior court approval.

The NYPD, which was not involved in the shooting, released body camera footage showing officers responding to the scene after the shooting. The FBI and Homeland Security Investigations are investigating the incident.

Mullin criticized Mamdani's anti-ICE rhetoric during a Friday news conference, accusing the mayor of inciting hostility toward federal immigration officers while refusing to support their enforcement efforts.

"His words are dangerous and incite hostility. It doesn't help," Mullin said. "He said that ICE is rotten to the core. Really? Men and women at ICE each day are enforcing the laws that he refuses to enforce. He said he wants to abolish ICE. Well, Mayor, if you abolish ICE, who's going to take the criminals off the streets of your own town?"

DHS told Fox News Digital that nearly 7,000 criminal illegal immigrants had been released from New York jurisdictions under sanctuary policies. The department said the Trump administration's immigration crackdown had resulted in more than 3 million illegal immigrants leaving the United States, including an estimated 2.2 million self-deportations.

item.title: Bill Maher reveals he's having dinner with Trump again, says he was 'really nice' by text
item.description: Liberal comedian Bill Maher revealed on his "Club Random" podcast that President Donald Trump invited him back for another White House dinner.
item.content:encoded:
Liberal comedian Bill Maher revealed on Monday that he's having dinner with President Donald Trump again.

"I'm having dinner with him again next week," Maher told famed Hollywood agent and executive Ari Emanuel during a conversation on Maher's "Club Random" podcast.

"After the first dinner, I went back to doing what I do... But then, like, he just, out of the blue, let's have dinner again. And I was like, great. And he was really nice," Maher said. "Like, I promise I won't say bad things about you like I did the last time.' And I texted back, and I said, 'You know what, you're the president of the United States. Say whatever the f--- you want. I'm just glad we're talking.' It's like being called a 'hockey puck' by Don Rickles. It's just what he does. It's how he talks."

BILL MAHER REVEALS TRUMP WAS 'GRACIOUS AND MEASURED' AT WHITE HOUSE MEETING, SAYS HE'S NOT THE MAN SEEN ON TV

Both Maher and Emanuel agreed it's better to talk with those they disagree with than not. Emanuel, who previously represented Trump when he hosted "The Apprentice," told Maher he had spoken with the president on "Monday."

"It blows my mind that there are people in this world and lots of them on the far left who just would turn this opportunity down, a private dinner in the White House with the president, just a few people, say whatever you want," Maher said. "I've heard people say, 'Well, I don't like the war.' Tell him! You can tell them, and I will."

Maher took swipes at Emanuel's client Larry David, who previously lambasted the HBO host for his White House dinner last year, while ignoring his agent's relationship with Trump.

"It's so interesting to me that Larry David, like, I'm the devil because I talk to him, but his own agent just talked to him on Monday," Maher laughed as Emanuel attempted to avoid weighing in. "You must recognize the hypocrisy there. Somehow, when it's his own agent doing the exact same thing, this is, then we don't play the Hitler card."

BILL MAHER FIRES BACK AT LARRY DAVID OVER 'MY DINNER WITH ADOLF' OP-ED, SAYS IT INSULTS '6 MILLION DEAD JEWS'

The podcast episode was released Monday but it is unclear whether the dinner has already happened. Neither the White House nor Maher's representatives responded to requests for comment.

Maher and Trump had been public foes for more than a decade until their mutual friend Kid Rock brokered a meeting between the two of them, which resulted in a dinner at the White House. He said during a monologue that Trump was more gracious and good-humored than he expected.

He also credited Trump for being "much more self-aware than he lets on in public," revealing the subject of the 2020 election came up during his tour of the White House and that he "didn't get mad" about how Maher brought up Trump's rare admission that he had lost.

MAHER MOCKS LIBERALS FOR STILL PANICKING ABOUT TRUMP'S ANTICS, PERSONALITY AFTER 10 YEARS

"Look, I get it. It doesn't matter who he is at a private dinner with a comedian. It matters who he is on the world stage. I'm just taking as a positive that this person exists. Because everything I've ever not liked about him was, I swear to God, absent at least on this night with this guy," Maher said. 

"I never felt I had to walk on eggshells around him," he told his audience. "And honestly, I voted for Clinton and Obama, but I would never feel comfortable talking to them the way I was able to talk with Donald Trump. That's just how it went down. Make of it what you will. Me? I feel it's emblematic of why the Democrats are so unpopular these days."

Their relationship appears to be in decent shape behind the scenes despite the public feuding since the dinner. Earlier this year, Maher received the Mark Twain Prize from the Kennedy Center, which Trump oversees as its chairman, and it's been reported that the White House attempted to block Maher from the award. Trump has also repeatedly attacked Maher's "low ratings" on Truth Social in recent months.

item.title: Judge Judy credits Her Honor program with making her 'hopeful' for the next generation
item.description: Judge Judy Sheindlin's Her Honor Mentoring program celebrates 20 years of empowering young women through mentorship and financial literacy skills.
item.content:encoded:
Judge Judy Sheindlin recently announced that she’s "rewiring" and letting son Adam Levy take the reins of TV courtroom drama, but she has plenty of other projects to keep her busy. The Her Honor Mentoring program she helped co-found just celebrated its 20-year anniversary.

Sheindlin founded the program with her daughter Nicole Sheindlin to empower young women through mentorship and professional development. For the past two decades, Her Honor Mentoring has welcomed approximately 2,500 participants; 1,500 mentees, selected from 31 high schools across the region, and more than 1,000 mentors from 400 organizations and businesses.

"I’m so happy to be here 20 years after our freshman year," Sheindlin told Fox News Digital.

The project, she said, "started off with a dream" and all they could do was hope it was successful. The first class held only eight or nine women, whereas the most recent class in September saw over 100.

JUDGE JUDY SHARES THE BEST PIECE OF PROFESSIONAL ADVICE SHE EVER RECEIVED AHEAD OF HER HONOR EVENT

"It’s the combination of the mentoring and the financial part of it – which is the girls get paid for working… and learning how to dress for success, learning about making first impressions, learning how to manage your money and just knowing how to grow up financially prepared to be an adult," Sheindlin told Fox News Digital.

The project, she said, is "simple, but satisfying." And she's been impressed and inspired by the young participants' drive to succeed.

"This small cohort makes me hopeful," Sheindlin said. "I think that you become jaded when you see so much dysfunction. I’ve been around so much adult dysfunction and juvenile dysfunction, that to see young people still hoping and dreaming, wanting to work hard to realize their dream that their journey on this Earth is positive and fulfilling, makes you feel good. It sort of renews your faith that probably the vast majority of people are like these young women. That they want their lives to be productive and happy and fulfilling."

Several of the former mentees have come back as mentors after starting their careers.

"We’re teaching them to give back," she said. "We’re teaching these young women the importance of being not only for themselves. But then once you’ve realized that, to supporting others with your time and your talent… they have a drive, they want to be their own engines. They want to be the engine that pulls their own train."

MORE GEN Z COLLEGE FRESHMEN ARE QUITTING SCHOOL EARLY AND MOVING BACK HOME WITH MOM AND DAD

JUDGE ADAM LEVY PREVIEWS HIS ‘NITTY-GRITTY’ NEW SHOW – AND HOW HIS STYLE COMPARES TO HIS MOM JUDGE JUDY

Sheindlin credited her stepdaughter Nicole as being "the engine that keeps the project running."

Nicole, the current CEO of Her Honor Mentoring, said the program started as a reflection of her relationship with Judge Judy. She went to the same law school as her stepmother and sat on the bench with her when she was a judge in family court. Nicole called it the perfect model for the program, saying, "The power and the impact of having a professional woman, a strong woman be a mentor, be a guide, be a supporter."

The mother-daughter duo concluded they should empower young women together to help women gain some extra skills and expand their professional network. 

"We’ve come to learn how much the mentors have grown and are inspired," Nicole told Fox Digital. "They’ve discovered that giving back empowers their own personal wellbeing."

The program connects mentees with mentors across several industries. During 20 weekly meetings throughout the academic year, mentoring teams explore topics related to education, career and financial literacy. 

In addition, as part of the Her Honor experience, mentees complete four electives. The offerings include field trips, digital courses and creative projects.

JUDGE JUDY HAS SCATHING MESSAGE FOR CITIES ENGULFED IN BRAZEN CRIME, PINPOINTS ‘RIDICULOUS’ POLICIES'

The 2026-27 Her Honor class consists of 108 mentees and 123 mentors across 14 schools throughout Bronx, Rockland and Westchester counties.

Mentee Keiry Alvarez and her mentor Lilliana Mendoza said they were grateful that the program helped them overcome their timidity. Alvarez, who said she was encouraged to join the program after her sister said Her Honor has helped her become more confident and outspoken.

Mendoza was the first generation female to go to college in her family and a 2016 Her Honor mentee. She said the program helped her combat her shyness, gain people skills and find her voice. She added that it gave her specific guidance that has made an impact on her career as a police officer in the Mamaroneck Police Department.

"Throughout my mentorship, I learned to have a lot of empathy for people and understand how people are, and I think that was a big part, because I also have a lot of empathy for people," she told Fox Digital.

item.title: British adventurer returns home after 28-year walk around the world
item.description: Adventurer Karl Bushby swam the English Channel and celebrated with fish and chips after his 28-year, 30,000-mile walk from Chile to England.
item.content:encoded:
Adventurer Karl Bushby has finally stepped foot on UK soil after a 28-year journey across the world.

On Oct. 5, he announced he swam the English Channel, from France to England. While resting in Dover, he said, "I’m staring at the Union Jack flying outside this hotel. I’ve seen many flags over the days, but that one is special."

On social media he shared one of his first meals back, overjoyed to have authentic British fish and chips again.

DALE 'GREY BEARD' SANDERS RECLAIMS TITLE AS OLDEST PERSON TO THRU-HIKE THE APPALACHIAN TRAIL AT 91

His journey is not over yet. He hopes to reach the finish line — his mother’s home in Hull — by the end of the month.

According to his website, he received a birthday card in the 1990s from his father about two soldiers arguing over an impossible feat, walking from London to New York via the Bering Strait. Karl grabbed a map and drew a single line, knowing he found his life’s mission.

NAVY VETERANS REUNITE AFTER 30 YEARS FOR 'GRUELING' CROSS-COUNTRY BIKE CHALLENGE HONORING 9/11

On Nov. 1, 1998, the ex-paratrooper started his journey in Chile, with only a few hundred dollars in his pocket "South America, you were young, it was all new, it was the boys adventure dream," Bushby said.

He walked north to the United States, waiting for the Bering Strait to freeze to cross from Alaska into Russia. In April 2012, Russia denied his next visa, pausing his expedition. So he started walking in the wrong direction, in protest, to the Russian Embassy in Washington, D.C. The ban was overturned and he carried on with his journey. From Russia he entered Mongolia, China, and swam the Caspian Sea from Kazakhstan to Azerbaijan.

Then it was on to Europe.

"You’ll find that you are way more capable than you think you are, people always underestimate themselves. The world always looks bigger and scarier than it actually is," Bushby said.

MAN WHO BEAT RARE CANCER CELEBRATES BY CANOEING 2,000 MILES WITH HIS DOG

He originally expected the journey to take 12 years, but visa restrictions, the 2008 financial crash, COVID-19, geopolitics, detention and some close calls slowed his progress. He says it’s the people that kept him going.

"The world is an incredible place, and it’s the people, the strangers that I have met along the way, that have kept me upright and moving forward," Bushby said.

Bushby has roughly 240 miles left to walk. He covered more than 30,000 miles, across 29 countries. "We went at a reasonable pace, we did what we needed to do and it has worked. I know it’s time to stop, I know that much because I feel that in the knees and ankles."

item.title: Ryan Seacrest's secrets for staying ripped at 51 without giving up wine, pizza or sweets
item.description: From curling heavy rocks on the beach to cinnamon buns at a local bakery, Ryan Seacrest shares the balanced fitness lifestyle behind his physique.
item.content:encoded:
Getting a shredded physique is apparently all about balance.

Last week, longtime "American Idol" host Ryan Seacrest showed off his flawless physique in an Instagram post, highlighting what a typical "day off" looks like for him.

The viral post, which showed him shirtless next to his bike, was met with applause and celebrity feedback. "Dancing with the Stars" pro Gleb Savchenko commented, "Let’s goo!!! Shredded."

NIGHTLY GLASS OF WINE MAY NOT BE AS HARMLESS AS MANY PEOPLE THINK, STUDY SUGGESTS

Actor and singer Nick Rashad Burroughs wrote, "This is what Ryan Seacrest looked like with a short off the whole time?!?"

In a response on Sunday, Seacrest posted a video to social media with the text, "What’s your idea of a perfect day?"

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

The video shows Seacrest gearing up for a scenic bike ride on the beach, featuring music and coffee. He then stops to curl and squat heavy rocks on the route.

After his morning workout, Seacrest visits a local bakery, commenting that cinnamon buns are "kind of my weakness."

Seacrest wrote in the caption of the post, "When I get free time away from work, it looks a lot like this. It’s health and enjoyment wrapped into one."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

The radio host shared how he aims to strike a balance in his lifestyle, like cycling 30 miles and stopping at the bakery on the way home.

"It’s gardening the produce and homemaking the pizza," he said. "It’s drinking the wine, and still making my workout the next day. Balance is not always a given, but it’s created."

Seacrest has previously shared his affinity for wellness and fitness, often posting photos and videos at the gym and on a bike.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Last month, he shared a video of himself working out with a variety of dumbbells and weight plates during a beach vacation.

The video featured resistance training combos, like squats paired with overhead dumbbell presses, and another including skull crushers with a barbell and reverse crunches.

Seacrest has shouted out his personal trainer, Dodd Romero, who famously trains other A-list celebrities like Lenny Kravitz and Jennifer Lopez.

Fox News Digital reached out to Seacrest and Romero for comment.

item.title: Pentagon data breach exposes records of over 3M people
item.description: The Pentagon data breach exposed 2.76 million Social Security numbers and military records, raising long-term identity theft concerns for veterans.
item.content:encoded:
You can change a password after a breach. You can cancel a credit card. But when your Social Security number gets exposed, you could be dealing with the fallout for years. That is the concern after a major breach involving the Pentagon's Defense Manpower Data Center. If you have served in the military, worked for the Department of War or have other ties to the military community, your information could be among the records involved.

A War Department official told CyberGuy that 2.76 million living individuals and 294,000 deceased individuals were affected. Depending on the person, the exposed information can include Social Security numbers, names, dates of birth, contact information and military personnel details. So, if a breach letter from the Pentagon shows up in your mailbox, don't toss it aside. Here's what happened, what may have been exposed and what you can do to protect yourself.

DMV BREACH CONFIRMED AS HACKERS CLAIM 200,000 RECORDS STOLEN

Join us for a free CyberGuy LIVE class.

Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson shares practical ways to stay safer, smarter and more confident with technology. Explore classes on stopping spam, phone security, financial protection and using AI to get better healthcare. Each class is free, easy to follow and comes with a free printable checklist.

See the classes and register at CyberGuyLive.com

The breach involved the Defense Manpower Data Center, or DMDC. A War Department official told CyberGuy that a DMDC information system experienced unauthorized access to personally identifiable information by a small number of unauthorized users between October 2025 and July 2026. The official said DMDC immediately remediated the vulnerability after discovering it. At this time, the department says it has no indication that the accessed information has been misused.

The files accessed contained unencrypted personally identifiable information. That created a potentially long exposure window before the vulnerability was discovered. Personal information such as a Social Security number can remain useful to criminals long after the original breach fades from the headlines.

The specific information varies depending on the person. According to the Pentagon, exposed records can include:

The military details make this breach particularly sensitive because the records may reveal more than basic identity information. DMDC plays a major role behind the scenes at the Department of Defense. It maintains more than 60 million records covering military personnel, civilian employees, contractors, family members, retirees and veterans. The agency uses those records to support benefits, identity verification and other Defense Department programs. In other words, plenty of people who left active military service years ago may still have information stored in these systems.

People whose personal information was accessed are being notified by postal mail through the Department's contracted provider, Identity Theft Guard Solutions, or IDX. If you receive a notice, read it carefully rather than assuming it is another piece of junk mail. The letter should explain what information tied to you was affected and what protection is being offered.

According to the War Department official, IDX is providing notification, credit monitoring and identity restoration support based on the data elements affected for each individual. Anyone with questions can visit response.idx.us/DMDC or call 1-855-744-4556.

Be careful with unexpected emails or text messages claiming to be connected to the breach. Scammers can use major security incidents as an excuse to send fake notices or links designed to steal even more information. Instead of clicking a link in an unexpected message, verify the information using the official IDX contact details or the postal notice you received.

WHY SCAMMERS TARGET VETERANS AND HOW TO FIGHT BACK

A credit card number has an expiration date. Your Social Security number usually stays with you for life. That can give criminals plenty of time to combine stolen information from one breach with information collected elsewhere. Someone might already have your phone number or an old email address. Adding a Social Security number and date of birth can make a stolen identity far more useful.

A criminal could try to open credit in your name or use the information in a convincing phishing attack. Other forms of identity fraud may never involve your credit report at all. That is why I would treat a breach involving an SSN differently from one exposing an email address or password.

A breach notice can leave you wondering where to start, so focus first on the protections that can limit what someone does with the information.

If DMDC sent you an official notification, review the identity protection services available to you. Eligible individuals may receive 12 months of free credit monitoring and identity restoration support through IDX, depending on the information affected. Credit monitoring can warn you about certain changes to your credit file. However, monitoring usually alerts you after activity occurs. It does not stop someone from attempting to use your identity.

If you were not contacted by DMDC, or if you want protection that continues beyond the free 12-month period, you may also want to consider a broader identity theft protection service. Depending on the service, it may monitor for suspicious use of your personal information and provide help if identity theft occurs. See my tips and best picks on Best Identity Theft Protection at CyberGuy.com.

Consider placing a credit freeze with Equifax, Experian and TransUnion. A freeze restricts access to your credit file, which can make it harder for someone to open a new credit account in your name. You can temporarily lift the freeze when you legitimately need to apply for credit. A freeze remains one of the strongest free steps you can take after your Social Security number has been exposed. Keep in mind that a freeze focuses on new credit. It cannot stop every type of identity theft, including fraud involving an existing account.

If you do not want to freeze your credit, you can place a fraud alert on your credit reports. A fraud alert tells lenders to take extra steps to verify your identity before opening new credit. You only need to contact one of the three major credit bureaus, and that bureau should notify the other two. A fraud alert offers less protection than a freeze, but it can still add another layer of scrutiny.

PENTAGON DATA BREACH EXPOSES SOCIAL SECURITY NUMBERS, PERSONAL INFO OF 2.76M US MILITARY, CIVILIAN PERSONNEL

Review your bank and credit card activity regularly. Also pay attention to unexpected changes involving accounts that use your identity. Turn on transaction alerts where available. Quick warnings can help you spot activity before it grows into a bigger problem.

Scammers pay attention to major data breaches too. You could receive a call, email or text from someone claiming to represent the Defense Department, a credit monitoring company or another organization offering to help you secure your identity.

Do not hand over a Social Security number, password or verification code because someone contacts you unexpectedly. Also avoid opening attachments or clicking links in unexpected breach-related messages.

Strong antivirus software can help detect malicious downloads, suspicious links and other threats that may show up in follow-up scams. Keep your security software updated and verify unexpected requests using official contact information you find yourself. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android and iOS devices at CyberGuy.com.

Turn on two-factor authentication (2FA) for your email, financial accounts and other important services whenever it is available. Your email account deserves special attention because criminals can use it to reset passwords for other accounts. An authenticator app or passkey can offer stronger protection than relying only on a password.

If your Social Security number was exposed, consider getting an IRS Identity Protection PIN. An IP PIN is a six-digit number that helps prevent someone else from filing a federal tax return using your Social Security number. The IRS issues a new PIN each year. This can be especially useful after a breach because tax-related identity theft may not show up on a credit report.

One year of free monitoring is useful, but stolen personal information does not become harmless when that year expires. Continue checking your credit reports and financial accounts. Also pay attention to unexpected tax notices, benefit claims or bills that you do not recognize. We have previously explained why a credit freeze alone does not stop every form of identity theft. A stolen Social Security number can potentially be misused in ways that never trigger a traditional credit check.

What stands out to me here is how long the information involved can remain valuable. A password can be replaced in a few minutes, but a Social Security number, birth date or military history can follow you for decades. If you receive one of these Pentagon breach notices, I would take it seriously even though officials say they have not seen evidence of misuse. Use the free monitoring being offered and consider freezing your credit. Then keep an eye on your accounts after that free monitoring period ends. We hand organizations an enormous amount of personal information because we often have no practical alternative. When that information gets exposed, the burden of watching for fraud suddenly falls back on us.

If the government loses information as sensitive as your Social Security number, should it be responsible for protecting your identity for longer than one year? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

item.title: Selma Blair arrested after in-flight incident
item.description: Selma Blair, 54, was arrested Sunday in New York after allegedly attacking crew members mid-air on a Delta flight from Los Angeles.
item.content:encoded:
Selma Blair was arrested Sunday after allegedly attacking crew members on board a Delta flight into New York City.

"On Sunday October 11 at approximately 11pm at JFK Airport, PAPD responded to a call about a physically abusive passenger aboard Delta Airlines flight 938 which was parked at the gate after arrival from LAX," New York Port Authority officials confirmed to Fox News Digital. 

"Suspect was identified as Selma Blair, a 54-year-old woman. She was taken into custody and transported to the hospital for evaluation."

A rep for Blair told TMZ, "Selma experienced a medical emergency that led to the alleged conduct. Upon landing, she received immediate medical attention and is currently in stable condition."

SELMA BLAIR SAYS ‘NO ONE RETURNED MY CALLS’ AFTER ANTI-ISLAM COMMENT LED TO HOLLYWOOD FALLOUT

Officials confirmed two flight attendants also reported injuries, and one was transported to the hospital for further evaluation. 

Delta confirmed that law enforcement officials responded to an incident upon arrival to John F. Kennedy International Airport, a flight which departed out of Los Angeles earlier in the day.

"Delta has zero tolerance for unruly or unlawful behavior, as the safety of our customers and crew always comes first," Delta said in a statement.

 Additionally, there was no operational impact to the flight as it landed ahead of schedule at JFK, Delta said. 

Blair's representatives did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. 

This is a developing story. Check back for updates.

item.title: Season is already over for these four NFL teams after Week 5, you can write them off now
item.description: The Miami Dolphins, Arizona Cardinals, Tennessee Titans, and Los Angeles Chargers are officially done, but several struggling NFL teams barely escape.
item.content:encoded:
Five weeks into the NFL season, we can officially write off four teams. By "write off," we mean teams that are going nowhere. Their fans should be more concerned with draft position than anything their teams might accomplish this season.

We understand how demoralizing it is to concede a season before mid-October. It is, nonetheless, the reality for certain franchises.

Let's start with two teams that aren't tanking, per se, but weren't exactly built to contend this season. The Miami Dolphins and Arizona Cardinals are about as bad as expected, despite the latter managing an early-season win.

The positive is that both teams have stockpiled young talent while positioning themselves for a high draft pick. Miami's rookie class is impressive, including Kadyn Proctor, Chris Johnson, Jacob Rodriguez, Caleb Douglas, and Chris Bell. Arizona has the best tight end in football in Trey McBride, while Jeremiah Love, albeit injured, has generational upside.

Unfortunately, the 2027 quarterback class doesn't appear nearly as promising as anticipated. Arch Manning, to this point, hardly resembles the prospect analysts projected him to become.

Elsewhere, the Tennessee Titans might be worse than both the Dolphins and Cardinals. That's particularly concerning because Tennessee spent the offseason actively trying to improve its roster and coaching staff.

Through Week 5, the Titans rank last in the NFL in both scoring and total offense, averaging just 11.6 points and 246.4 yards per game.

The winless Titans shouldn't be expected to win many games this season.

After five weeks, we can also write off the Los Angeles Chargers, who entered the season with nearly the same Super Bowl odds as the Kansas City Chiefs. A team coached by Jim Harbaugh and quarterbacked by Justin Herbert should not be this inept. And yet, they are.

At 0-5, with games remaining against the Rams, Ravens, Chiefs twice, 49ers, and Patriots, it's difficult to find many wins left on the schedule.

A midseason parting with offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel now seems more plausible than a late-season surge toward the playoffs. The Chargers' season, at least in terms of meaningful aspirations, is over.

Based strictly on their play, the New Orleans Saints and Tampa Bay Buccaneers should join this list. Both teams have won just one game and have deficiencies on both sides of the ball. Despite relatively high expectations entering the season, the Saints have a minus-33 point differential.

Neither team figures to be much of a factor in the postseason, if it gets there at all. However, both remain just one game out of first place in the perpetually mediocre NFC South.

Likewise, the 1-3-1 Washington Commanders remain viable playoff threats largely because of the lackluster state of the rest of the NFC East.

Granted, it's hard to take seriously a team that did that in overtime on Sunday

The 2-3 New York Jets are the final team worth discussing. As WWE commentator Michael Cole told OutKick last week, the Jets remain poorly coached and overmatched in the trenches. In all likelihood, they are probably a bottom-10 team in the NFL–again.

But we can't, in good faith, write off a team that sits just one game behind the Patriots and Bills, who play the Rams on Monday night, in the AFC East.

We suspect the Jets will join this list by the end of October. For now, however, they've played well enough — including competitive games against the Lions and Packers — to keep the light on for a few more weeks.

So, through Week 5, the Dolphins, Cardinals, Titans, and Chargers are the only four teams we're officially declaring "season over."

The rest of the fan bases should at least have hope, even for just a short while longer.

item.title: Biden-appointed judge with history of fiery Trump clashes erupts at DOJ: 'You've lost all credibility!'
item.description: Judge Ana Reyes screamed at government lawyers over 430 trees cut down at East Potomac Golf Links, demanding answers about late Friday notification.
item.content:encoded:
A Biden-appointed federal judge who previously drew a formal misconduct complaint from President Donald Trump's Justice Department for alleged bias erupted at government lawyers again Monday, in a heated showdown over rapid tree removal at a historic golf course on national parkland.

Judge Ana Reyes unleashed her latest rebuke during an emergency hearing over hundreds of trees removed from East Potomac Golf Links in Hains Point, D.C. Trump wants to transform the historic public facility into a championship-caliber golf course like his courses in the U.S., Ireland and Scotland – the latest courtroom collision between the administration and its political opponents.

Journalist Scott MacFarlane, who live-tweeted from the hearing, described Reyes as "scream[ing]" at administration attorneys over the government's late-Friday notification that tree removal would begin Saturday. A government lawyer acknowledged that approximately 430 trees had already been cut down, according to MacFarlane.

OBAMA-APPOINTED JUDGE TORCHES TRUMP ADMIN IN LATEST COURTROOM SHOWDOWN, REFERS ATTORNEY FOR BAR REVIEW

"You've lost credibility!" Reyes told government attorneys, according to MacFarlane's live courtroom reporting.

The administration maintains that the removals implement a 2019 National Park Service landscape-restoration plan predating Trump's redesign proposal for the links, which sit on an island connected to the city proper by the Jefferson Memorial and Francis Case Bridge at its western edge.

BIDEN-APPOINTED JUDGE ORDERS TRUMP TO RESTORE SLAVERY, CLIMATE CHANGE REFERENCES AT NATIONAL PARKS

Reyes, who was born in Uruguay and nominated by Biden in 2023, previously grilled a Trump administration attorney about his religious beliefs during litigation challenging Trump's restrictions on transgender military service — an order she called "biologically inaccurate" according to the Washington Post.

The judge questioned how Jesus Christ would respond to "telling a group of people that they are so worthless, so worthless that we’re not going to allow them into homeless shelters?" according to then-DOJ Chief of Staff Chad Mizelle’s complaint.

EXCLUSIVE: TRUMP’S DC JUDICIAL NEMESIS TARGETED IN MISCONDUCT COMPLAINT OVER ALLEGED BIDEN DOJ TIES

In a 2025 case, Reyes ruled that Trump violated federal notice requirements when he fired several inspectors general but then declined to reinstate them, according to Reuters.

Monday's hearing brought another heated exchange, this time over when government lawyers learned of the tree-removal operation and why they waited until the end of the workweek to notify the court.

"At 4:55pm on a Friday of a holiday weekend, the plaintiffs and I get [little] notice that hundreds of trees are going to be chopped down," Reyes reportedly fumed at the government, according to MacFarlane.

EXCAVATION SET TO BEGIN ON TRUMP ADMINISTRATION'S 250-FOOT TRIUMPHAL ARCH AMID LEGAL BATTLE

When government counsel reportedly acknowledged learning of the operation on Oct. 8 or 9 and said officials were awaiting details, Reyes demanded:

"Do you have email or a cell phone?"

MacFarlane tweeted that he had never heard a judge "scream at full-voice at a lawyer before," while the UK Independent reported Reyes excoriated federal counsel for about 15 minutes.

The uproar comes as preservationists and progressive interests challenge the administration, including former Obama ethics lawyer Norm Eisen — who has engineered a "broad legal resistance" to the president through his group Democracy Defenders Fund, according to its mission statement.

Eisen tweeted a victory lap Monday after the court agreed to hear the case in an "emergency’ setting.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Preservationists argued the administration has not satisfied applicable environmental and historic-preservation requirements.

The administration disputed that argument, maintaining that the tree removal is authorized NPS landscape management separate from Trump's proposed links renovation.

item.title: America’s most rat-infested cities ranked as Midwest surprise cracks top 10
item.description: The city of Detroit cracked Terminix's top 10 most rodent-infested cities for the first time, joining New York City, Los Angeles and Philadelphia on the annual list.
item.content:encoded:
A national pest control company has released its annual list of the top 10 most rodent-infested cities in the U.S. — and one Midwest city has now joined the list for the first time.

The list is based on rodent control service data from more than 300 Terminix branches nationwide in 2025, ranking cities where residents most frequently used the company's services.

While New York and Los Angeles held onto the top two spots, Philadelphia moved up one spot to No. 3.

'MASSIVE' RAT SPOTTED RUNNING THROUGH AIRPLANE FORCES CANCELLATION OF VACATION FLIGHT

The top 10 list included returning cities like Houston, Chicago and Washington, D.C. — as well as Boston and Dallas.

There was also a new entrant in the top 10 this year.

For the first time, Detroit cracked the top 10, moving up one spot from No. 11.

Rodent infestations have previously raised concerns among Detroit residents.

POPULAR SUMMER DESTINATION RAVAGED BY LYME DISEASE BETS ON RADICAL NEW SOLUTION

In a 2023 memorandum obtained by Fox News Digital, Detroit Mayor Mary Sheffield, who was then serving as the city council president, said residents complained about rodent infestations during a community meeting.

"In a recent community meeting that I held, rodent infestations were a main complaint among our residents," Sheffield said at the time.

"[Residents] shared that many demolition properties become homes for rat infestation."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Fox News Digital reached out to Sheffield's office for comment.

Following Detroit on the list were Hartford, Atlanta, Baltimore, Tampa and Sacramento, rounding out the top 15.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Terminix said all the cities on the list share three common factors: large populations, abundant food sources and plenty of places for rodents to hide.

"Together, these conditions give rats and mice the resources they need to survive and reproduce," said Terminix in a release. The Rentokil Terminix company is headquartered in Memphis, Tennessee. 

"Large populations generate significant amounts of food waste, while dumpsters, alleys, parks, and other urban spaces can give rodents easy access to food," the company added.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"Older buildings, subway systems, and sewer networks provide additional places to travel, hide, and nest."

Terminix also urged residents to take steps to prevent rodent infestations. 

That includes sealing cracks and openings around doors, windows and foundations, storing food in airtight containers and keeping living spaces clean and free of crumbs and food residue.

"If you live in one of the most rat-infested cities, these steps can significantly help lower the risk of a rodent infestation," the company added.

item.title: Republican lawmakers break with Trump on diesel deal with Russia
item.description: Some Republican lawmakers voiced staunch opposition after United States President Donald Trump announced a diesel agreement with Russia.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump last week touted a diesel agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin, asserting that prices for the fuel would swiftly fall, but some Republicans have responded by rebuking the president's move.

"I have just concluded a highly successful discussion with President Vladimir Putin, of Russia, wherein it was agreed that Russia will immediately supply over 300,000 Tons of Diesel Fuel to the American and Global Marketplace, another 500,000 Tons during the month of November, and 1,000,000 Tons immediately thereafter. Additionally, based on the condition of their Diesel Refineries, Russia will then deliver, within a short period of time, 3,000,000 Tons of Diesel Fuel," Trump declared in an Oct. 9 Truth Social post.

"Between our TOTAL CONTROL of the Strait of Hormuz, and this great announcement on Russian Energy, Diesel Prices for Americans and, indeed, the World, will be COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST! Lower prices for Americans, especially our Great Farmers, Ranchers, and Truckers, is my Greatest Priority. This is a very big and important announcement. Additionally, it must be understood, that Iran will not have a Nuclear Weapon!" Trump declared.

The announcement sparked blowback from some Republicans, including outgoing Rep. Don Bacon of Nebraska, who declared in a post on X that Trump's "policies towards Russia and Ukraine are failures."

ZELENSKYY ACCUSES PUTIN OF DEFYING TRUMP'S CEASEFIRE PUSH, SENDS POINTED MESSAGE TO WHITE HOUSE

"Propping up Putin’s war economy is morally wrong as he uses that money to bomb cities," Bacon asserted. "We need moral clarity not moral ambiguity."

Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick, R-Pa., declared in a post on Saturday, "We will be introducing bipartisan legislation to block any and all purchases of Russian oil. It will be called the 'Ronald Reagan Peace Through Strength Act.' It will be forced to the Floor via discharge and it will pass overwhelmingly."

Bacon shared Fitzpatrick's post and noted, "I’ve already agreed to be an original cosponsor. Congress must make a stand."

A bipartisan group of senators — including Democratic Sens. Jeanne Shaheen of New Hampshire, Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut, Ron Wyden of Oregon, as well as GOP Sens. Susan Collins of Maine, Lisa Murkowski of Alaska, Thom Tillis of North Carolina and John Curtis of Utah — joined together in a statement pressing the administration to "reverse course."

"Congress explicitly banned Russian energy imports in 2022 to prevent American dollars from financing Putin’s brutal war against Ukraine. Congress was clear: The U.S. should not import oil from Russia until it ends its aggression against Ukraine and ceases threats against our NATO Allies," the statement declares.

TRUMP RUSSIA DEAL COULD FUEL PUTIN'S WAR, EX-NATO COMMANDER WARNS AS ZELENSKYY SAYS 'NYET'

"President Trump’s decision to allow Russian diesel imports to the U.S. runs directly counter to that law. The Administration has also failed to consult with Congress or submit any explanation to justify its decision as required by statute. The United States should not provide Putin with a financial lifeline while Russia continues to kill Ukrainian civilians. The Administration must immediately reverse course," the statement adds.

Tillis, an outgoing senator who is not seeking re-election, is the author of the recently released book, "How to Lose Friends and Antagonize Presidents." Shaheen is also not seeking another term.

Former U.S. Energy Secretary Dan Brouillette explained during a Monday appearance on FOX Business that he does not expect the agreement to cause the price of diesel to decline significantly.

He said that he believes "it's important for Americans to realize that ... we may not be talking about brand new barrels to the marketplace. So, if there's an expectation that prices are gonna come down dramatically as a result of this agreement, I'm a bit skeptical of that."

TRUMP CALLS FOR UKRAINE TO REPLACE ZELENSKYY AFTER CLASH OVER RUSSIA DIESEL DEAL: 'GET A NEW PRESIDENT'

Brouillette said that if the aim is to decrease "prices in the long term," then it is "challenging to see how this is going to help. What we're in essence doing is rearranging the barrels," Brouillette explained, "we're moving the barrels from one customer to another customer. We're not producing new barrels of diesel, which is really what the market is expecting and wanting."

Fox News Digital reached out to the White House on Monday.

item.description: First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli says Chinese espionage is "extremely pervasive" after his office charged alleged spies in recent months.
item.content:encoded:
First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli said Chinese espionage is "extremely pervasive" in the U.S. following the arrest of an alleged Chinese agent in Los Angeles this month.

Essayli told Fox News Digital in an interview that his office has pressed charges against several alleged Chinese spies in recent months, saying Beijing is brazen in its attempts to build their access inside the U.S.

"I think it's extremely pervasive," Essayli said of Chinese spying. "China is one of our biggest adversaries, and they're committed to advancing their interests. And they're playing the long game, and so they are willing to put a lot of resources into developing sources, recruiting people within the U.S. to advance their interests.

CHINA EXPERT WARNS BEIJING WANTS AMERICANS — NOT THE CCP — TO SPREAD ITS MESSAGE

"They're willing to steal our technology; they're willing to engage in espionage here. So, there's no limit to what China is willing to do. It is a huge, huge concern. We have to be vigilant, and we have to disrupt these operations on our soil," Essayli said. "We have to protect our sovereignty."

"If you look at just the cases we brought this year, just in my office, I mean, you had cases where the woman from Irvine was engaged in espionage against the Taiwanese president's family member. I had a guy last week we arrested, he sold more than $300 million in SI chips, formerly known as AI chips, to China," he continued. "You had a mayor of a local city that we charged for serving as an unregistered agent of China as well, pushing out their propaganda and taking orders from China."

FORMER CALIFORNIA MAYOR ADMITS TO SECRETLY WORKING FOR CHINA, SPREADING BEIJING PROPAGANDA IN US

"So, it's extremely pervasive. It's a huge problem, but the FBI is on it," he said. "They have entire squads dedicated to combating this, and we're committed here at the U.S. Attorney's Office to supporting those investigations and bringing criminal charges to disrupt these operations."

Wanying Zhang, 34, of Irvine, was arrested earlier this month for allegedly working with an associate to photograph and record the family outside their Seattle-area home, according to a criminal complaint obtained by Fox News Digital.

CHINA-LINKED HACKERS INFILTRATED US GOVERNMENT NETWORKS BEFORE FBI TAKEDOWN

Authorities nabbed Zhang, who goes by "Heather" in the U.S., at the Los Angeles airport as she attempted to board a plane to China.

Essayli said FBI Los Angeles agents arrested Zhang on a federal charge of acting as an unregistered agent of the People’s Republic of China.

CALIFORNIA MAYOR ACCUSED OF SECRETLY WORKING FOR CHINA, SPREADING PROPAGANDA WHILE IN OFFICE: FEDS

She allegedly traveled to Seattle in 2025 at the direction of Chinese officials and sent them photos, videos and license plate information.

"She coordinated the trip with an associate and used tradecraft to avoid detection," Essayli wrote. "She never notified the attorney general she was acting for a foreign government, a federal offense."

GOOGLE ENGINEER STOLE AI SECRETS FOR CHINA, SENATE HEARS IN EXPLOSIVE TESTIMONY

Speaking on "The Big Weekend Show" Sunday, Essayli said Zhang is a naturalized U.S. citizen and confirmed the alleged surveillance targeted a relative of Taiwan’s president.

"She was conducting surveillance on behalf of the Chinese government. She was acting as a foreign agent," Essayli said. "And she was spying on a relative of the president of Taiwan here in the U.S."

The alleged target was Ting-Yu Lai, the U.S.-based son of Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te, CBS News reported, citing law enforcement sources. The complaint does not name him.

"Saw him. Young male. It’s that young one," Zhang allegedly messaged a Chinese government contact while outside the home.

"I am video recording," she allegedly added before sending two license plate numbers.

item.title: Leon Slater enters league of his own as he captures TNA World Championship at Bound for Glory
item.description: Leon Slater survived a Fame-asser and Skull Crushing Finale to capture the TNA World Championship, becoming the youngest champion in TNA history.
item.content:encoded:
The Total Nonstop Action Wrestling (TNA) World Championship is the top prize in the company and adding your name to the rich legacy of the title is a worthy cause for any pro wrestler.

The pressure is enough for anyone, but add a shot at history on top of it is almost too much. It was what Leon Slater was trying to accomplish at Bound for Glory on Sunday night in Tampa, Florida. If Slater defeated Nic Nemeth, he would become the youngest TNA world champion in the promotion’s history at 22 years old. The opportunity came months after Slater nearly became the longest-reigning X Division champion.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE

Pressure can crush anyone who cannot live up to it. It can also make diamonds.

Slater survived a Skull Crushing Finale and a Rough Ryder. He superkicked Nemeth and got his opponent in position for the Swanton 450. He hit the move but Nemeth kicked out of the pin. He tried again, but Nemeth got his knees up and nearly pinned him in the same sequence.

Nemeth hit a Danger Zone and tried to pin Slater, but to no avail.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Slater dug as deep as he could. He countered every chance Nemeth had to move out of the way of the danger Slater brought with him. Slater went over the turnbuckle and onto the floor to catch Nemeth slipping. As he tossed Nemeth back into the ring, Nemeth moved out of the way of a third Swanton 450. Instead, Slater soared across the ring and nailed a splash.

It set Slater up for the final Swanton 450. He hit it perfectly and pinned Nemeth for the win.

Slater became the youngest TNA world champion and proved that the "Youngest in Charge" was certainly that.

Nemeth’s reign ends at 105 days. It was his second reign as world champion.

Now, Slater has the title and has etched his name into the TNA history books.

item.title: Bright lights not too bright for the Brewers or superfan Front Row Amy in Game 1 of NLCS
item.description: Jacob Misiorowski and the bullpen held the Los Angeles Dodgers to one run as the Milwaukee Brewers took NLCS Game 1 while Front Row Amy went viral.
item.content:encoded:
Those who thought the Los Angeles Dodgers and their massive payroll were going to waltz into Milwaukee and run over the Brewers were wrong. This is a team that won 103 games this season for the best record in baseball.

They're not going to forget how to play the game now that October and its bright lights have arrived. They have too much talent for that, and they proved that in a 2-1 win in Game 1 of the NLCS.

The lights aren’t too bright for the Brew Crew or their superfan, Amy Williams, better known as Front Row Amy. They showed up, proved that they weren't going to be run over and took a tight Game 1 while she went viral.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Brewers ace Jacob Misiorowski was on the mound. He gave up one run in 4 1/3 innings of work before turning it over to the bullpen to hold it down the rest of the way, which they did.

They only needed two runs and that's what they ended up with when the final out in the top of the ninth was recorded. All you have to do in October is win. It doesn’t matter how, just score more runs than the other team.

BREWERS STUN DODGERS, 2-1, IN NLCS GAME 1 AS LA'S OFFENSE FLOPS WITH RUNNERS IN SCORING POSITION

Misiorowski did his job. The bullpen did its job. The bats did their job. And Front Row Amy was behind the plate as she is for most Brewers games doing her job. That's winning baseball.

Now isn’t the time to pump the brakes. The work isn't finished.

The Dodgers are back-to-back World Series champs for a reason. You have to show up to each and every game in this series ready to match the intensity of the postseason.

I've seen enough baseball to know that showing up prepared for the intensity of the postseason isn't going to be a problem for Front Row Amy. She shows up each and every time out.

It's the rest of the Brewers that you have to worry about if you're a fan. That said, they're off to a good start in this series. They're not the same team that got swept by the Dodgers in last season's NLCS.

Game 2 is at 5 p.m., Monday.

item.title: Amazing Red enters TNA Hall of Fame and wins X Division Championship on same night at Bound for Glory
item.description: Amazing Red stunned a seven-man scramble to capture the TNA X Division Championship for the fourth time after his Hall of Fame speech entrance.
item.content:encoded:
The X Division Championship scramble was simply "amazing."

The match was initially billed as a six-man match among BDE, KC Navarro, Ryan Nemeth, Fabian Aichner, Rich Swann and Cedric Alexander. The X Division title was vacated when Leon Slater cashed in "Option C" for a shot at the TNA World Championship.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE

Amazing Red was being inducted into the TNA Hall of Fame as part of a class that included Konnan and ODB. He said during his speech he would enter the match Sunday night at Bound for Glory. The six-man scramble turned into a seven-man brawl. Chaos was everywhere in the ring. Amazing Red knew better than anyone what it took to win the X Division title.

Swann and BDE were unfazed at first. The duo used their tag team skills to keep Amazing Red grounded for the most part. It appeared it could have been one of their nights to live in infamy.

KC Navarro also thought he was going to score the victory. He hit the 305 on Aichner and followed it up with a Blessing in Disguise. But as he went to pin Aichner, Nemeth pulled the referee out of the ring. Navarro would hit the floor and take out Nemeth.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Navarro reentered the ring and came face-to-face with his hero – Amazing Red.

The veteran, however, got the advantage. Amazing Red connected with a Spanish Fly and followed it up with the Code Red. Amazing Red pinned Navarro and scored the victory, capturing the X Division Championship.

It’s the fourth time Amazing Red has held the title, but it’s been quite some time. The last time he held the X Division Championship was all the way back in September 2010. He won it at a live event but dropped it to Jay Lethal only a few days later.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

Amazing Red’s fourth reign is good for eighth-best in the title’s history. Chris Sabin (10), Austin Aries (6), Jay Lethal (6), A.J. Styles (6), Samoa Joe (5), Low Ki (5) and Frankie Kazarian (5) have only held the belt more times than him.

item.title: Indi Hartwell gets back to top of women's wrestling, captures TNA Knockouts Championship at Bound for Glory
item.description: Indi Hartwell defeated Xia Brookside at TNA Bound for Glory after special guest referee Mickie James played a pivotal role in the title match.
item.content:encoded:
Indi Hartwell never lost her WWE NXT Championship when she was with the company. She was only forced to relinquish the title when she was drafted to the Raw brand.

On Sunday, Hartwell was back on top of a women’s division in pro wrestling. She defeated Xia Brookside at Total Nonstop Action Wrestling’s (TNA) Bound for Glory pay-per-view to become the Knockouts world champion for the first time in her career.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE

Hartwell worked hard to get back into the Knockouts World Championship picture. She nearly got her first taste of TNA gold in the Knockouts TV Championship Tournament, but was eliminated in the semifinals. She dusted herself off and continued to vie for the illusive belt, picking up a tag team title win with Harley Hudson and winning a match via DQ against Zoey Serrano.

After Daria Rae slapped her backstage, Hartwell was rewarded with a shot at the Knockouts Championship against Brookside. Brookside and Hartwell both explained in their pre-match promos the match essentially came down to doing things the right way.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Brookside did her damndest to keep the title but her frustrations got the better of her. She slapped special guest referee Mickie James twice before the TNA Hall of Famer retaliated. Hartwell took advantage and hit the Hurts Donut to get the win.

Brookside’s reign ends after 105 days. She initially won the title against Lei Ying Lee.

Hartwell is the fourth different Knockout to win the belt this year, following in the footsteps of Brookside, Lee and Arianna Grace.

Hartwell is a champion again and there doesn’t seem to be anyone who is going to take that belt away from her immediately.

item.title: Jason Hotch captures TNA International Championship at Bound for Glory as Order 4 disintegrates
item.description: Jason Hotch stunned Mustafa Ali with a crucifix pin to recapture the TNA International Championship as Order 4's brutal war reached its climax.
item.content:encoded:
Order 4 went to war on Sunday night at Bound for Glory.

The faction that had a chokehold on the Total Nonstop Action Wrestling (TNA) roster for quite some time completely disintegrated in recent weeks leading to all four male members getting into a match for Mustafa Ali’s TNA International Championship.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE

Ali tried to defend it against Jason Hotch, John Skyler and Special Agent 0. Each man showcased their athletic abilities. Special Agent 0 dove over the ropes to knock down all three of his opponents. But his momentum came to a screeching halt. Ali, Hotch and Skyler teamed together for a few minutes to get Special Agent 0 on a table outside of the ring.

Tasha Steelz tried to step in and prevent any damage. Mila Moore, who was in Skyler’s corner, had different ideas. She hit Steelz with her heel and knocked her onto the table beside Special Agent 0. Ali then went to the top rope and hit a nasty 450 splash through the table.

It was up to Ali, Hotch and Skyler from there on. Skyler nailed a double destroyer on his opponents. But the two top stars in Order 4 showed just how good they were.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Hotch took out Special Agent 0 one last time, hitting a double stomp from the top rope. Ali was waiting for him on the opposite turnbuckle.

Ali hit Hotch with a 450 splash, but Hotch rolled up Ali with a sudden crucifix pin. He picked up the win and was crowned the new TNA international champion.

It is the second TNA International Championship reign for Hotch. He initially defeated Ali back on "Impact" in July. But Ali regained the title once their alliance broke apart, defeating Hotch at Lockdown.

As Order 4 fell to the wayside, Hotch got back on top.

He only held the title for 24 days the first time. He’s likely expecting a much longer reign coming out of Bound for Glory.
